title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker7-edhoc: transcript_3/4 incorrectly CBOR-encodes plaintext — TH_3/TH_4 diverge from RFC 9529
description:
## Summary

`transcript_3` and `transcript_4` apply `encode_bstr` to their plaintext inputs, treating them as single CBOR bstr data items. Per RFC 9529 test vectors, PLAINTEXT_2/PLAINTEXT_3 are CBOR sequences (not bstr data items) and must be concatenated raw into the transcript hash — not wrapped in an additional bstr layer.

## Evidence

RFC 9529 Section 2.3 defines TH_3 input as the CBOR sequence:

```
CBOR(TH_2) || PLAINTEXT_2_raw || CBOR(CRED_R)
```

where `PLAINTEXT_2` = `41 18 [C_R] a1 18 22... [ID_CRED_R] 58 40... [signature]` (82 raw bytes, no additional bstr wrapper).

The current code produces:
```
CBOR(TH_2) || CBOR(PLAINTEXT_2) || CBOR(CRED_R)
```

Which adds 2 extra bytes to PLAINTEXT_2 and potentially more to CRED_R (if already CBOR-encoded).

## Impact

- TH_3 computed by code (`cf726a92...`) ≠ RFC 9529 TH_3 (`5b7df9b4...`)
- TH_4 similarly diverges
- All downstream derived values (PRK_out, PRK_exporter, OSCORE params) are inconsistent with the RFC
- Interoperability with RFC-compliant EDHOC implementations is broken

## Affected code

- `rust/lichen-oscore/src/edhoc.rs`: `transcript_3` (L529), `transcript_4` (L538) — both use `encode_bstr` on plaintext and cred
- `python/src/lichen/crypto/edhoc.py`: analogous TH_3/TH_4 computation at L626-629, L657-661

## Fix direction

`transcript_3` and `transcript_4` should:
1. `encode_bstr` on TH_2 (correct — TH_2 is a bstr data item)
2. Append plaintext raw (no bstr wrapper — it is a CBOR sequence)
3. Append credential raw if already CBOR-encoded, or `encode_bstr` if raw bytes
4. `transcript_2` fix (this commit) is already correct

## Pre-existing

This bug predates commit `b5f641ef6d`. The same commit correctly fixed `transcript_2` but `transcript_3`/`transcript_4` were already using `encode_bstr` on plaintext before the fix and remain incorrect.
